14:55 Local Time, 09:55 GMT, 15:25 IST: It's tea time in Rawalpindi with the covers firmly in place. Had been Pakistan's session in the morning with Saqib Khan's 7 for 130 stealing the spotlight. Both Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis were dismissed early and the rest of the Sri Lankan batting crumbled. Saqib was unrelenting with his line and length and his burst ensured that the visitors managed only a 12-run lead. The hosts lost Tayyab Arif early in the second innings, but this pair has ensured that they're slightly ahead. Bad light then played spoilsport and with only 4 sessions remaining, it's hard to see a result from this match. Will we get any more cricket post-tea? It does look doubtful, but we'll be back with updates as it comes along.

Will either of the two teams try and conjure up a result tomorrow? Or will the match end in a drab draw? We'll be back at 9:20 am for all the action on the final day of this Test. 16:19 Local Time, 11:19 GMT, 16:49 IST: The match is drawn as the players shake hands. What an innings from Saud Shakeel, but he will be disappointed for not crossing the 3 figure mark once again in the match. Sri Lankan bowlers started off well today by striking off the first ball, but the partnership between Saud Shakeel and Ghori for the 7th wicket, brought them back into the game. Shakeel held one end together with a gritty knock, but was unlucky to get a ton. Both teams will be happy with the way their middle order responded after the initial setback. For, Pakistan, the debutants performed well, with Saqib Khan getting a 7-fer to trigger the Sri Lankan collapse. Tayyab got to his fifty, but didn't make it count with a big one. The new skipper for Sri Lanka, Kusal Mendis got to a ton and gave good company to DDS, who went on to make a big hundred, which was instrumental in the Sri Lankan revival. We lost more than 120 overs in this Test match and as such draw was the only realistic result possible. There were positives for both teams: the four debutants acquitted themselves pretty well for the hosts while Sri Lanka's middle-order batted with authority, as did their pace bowlers. The second Test will start on the 17th and the venue has been shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi. With bad light being a factor, will both teams agree to play it with a pink ball? Going by Babar Azam's post-match revelations, that looks unlikely. Light will certainly be a factor and we could be heading to a situation where one team must play out of their skins to get a positive result. We'll be back on Tuesday, though, with the hope of another good Test match. For now, cheers and bye..
